correlation_analysis.analysis_summary: The analysis focused on directly mapping log events to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, prioritizing the retrieved techniques. High confidence mappings were prioritized, with a focus on semantic similarity and clear attack patterns. Several events related to registry access and log clearing were successfully mapped. Events without clear matches were added to the unmapped_events list.

direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: The event description directly matches the technique description, indicating an attempt to remove evidence of malicious activity.
recommendations: Implement stricter access controls for event log clearing.
Monitor for unauthorized attempts to clear event logs.

direct_mappings.event_description: The System log file was cleared.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: The event description directly matches the technique description, indicating an attempt to remove evidence of malicious activity.
recommendations: Implement stricter access controls for event log clearing.
Monitor for unauthorized attempts to clear event logs.

direct_mappings.event_description: A new process has been created: reg.exe querying the registry.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: The event indicates the use of reg.exe to query the registry, which aligns with the technique of modifying or interacting with the Windows Registry for reconnaissance or other purposes.
recommendations: Monitor registry queries from unusual processes.
Investigate the purpose of the registry query.

direct_mappings.event_description: An attempt was made to duplicate a handle to an object.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Handle duplication involving reg.exe suggests potential manipulation or access to sensitive registry resources, aligning with the 'Modify Registry' technique.
recommendations: Investigate the target object of the handle duplication.
Monitor for unusual handle duplication activity.

direct_mappings.event_description: The handle to an object was closed related to reg.exe.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Handle closure related to reg.exe and registry keys, in conjunction with other registry access events, suggests potential registry manipulation.
recommendations: Correlate this event with other registry access events.
Investigate the registry key that was accessed.

direct_mappings.event_description: A handle to an object was requested to registry key by reg.exe.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Handle request related to reg.exe and registry keys, in conjunction with other registry access events, suggests potential registry manipulation.
recommendations: Correlate this event with other registry access events.
Investigate the registry key that was accessed.

direct_mappings.event_description: An attempt was made to access an object, specifically a registry key by reg.exe.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Registry key access by reg.exe suggests potential manipulation or information gathering, aligning with the 'Modify Registry' technique.
recommendations: Monitor registry access from unusual processes.
Investigate the specific registry key being accessed.

direct_mappings.event_description: Process accessed: Explorer.EXE accessing cmd.exe and powershell.exe
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Explorer.exe spawning cmd.exe and powershell.exe can be indicative of malicious activity leveraging PowerShell for command execution.
recommendations: Monitor process creation events for unusual parent-child relationships.
Investigate the commands being executed by PowerShell.

direct_mappings.event_description: Registry value set by Explorer.EXE in UserAssist key.
direct_mappings.mapping_rationale: Modifying the UserAssist key by Explorer.EXE can be used for persistence or to track user activity, aligning with the 'Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder' technique.
recommendations: Monitor modifications to the UserAssist registry key.
Investigate the purpose of the registry value being set.

overall_recommendations: Implement stricter access controls for event log clearing and registry modifications.
Monitor for unusual process creation events and registry access patterns.
Investigate any instances of Explorer.exe spawning command-line interpreters.
